items.title: Sonny Igoe interviewed by Monk Rowe, Emerson, New Jersey, July 31, 2003
items.q: So he brought some guys up and they let me jam with them.

ctx.x: I didn’t have any stool or something. Anyway but that’s what my set was the pits. Everybody else had great drums. So anyway I had had the good fortune to have met a fellow named Joe Mooney who was a marvelous musician from Paterson. He was blind. He played accordion like you never heard. It sounded like a brass section when he played the accordion. It was just great. He was a marvelous arranger. And my mother had a Hammond organ. My mother was a fine pianist. She had a Hammond organ when they first came out. And…

about Bobby Domenick. He sat right next to me and said, “listen” [scats] and I was like — I tell you I played with those guys, it was marvelous. And they taught me how to keep time. They really were great with me. They were so tolerant. I say I thought everybody loved me, but I don’t know how I sounded, really. But they were tolerant. They asked me to play all the time. So then we go to this contest. So Gene finally decides, I asked him to sign my snare drum for luck, you know you get it autographed. And I had…
